intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group sessions here, combining gentle movement with breathtaking natural views to start your day mindfully.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful stretches of coastline. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Surf instructors are plentiful and affordable along the beach.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-famous yoga culture at The Yoga Barn in Ubud, one of the most respected wellness centers in Southeast Asia. Drop-in classes cover Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, and meditation. With 13 days available, attending multiple sessions here is a transformative highlight of any Bali trip.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Snorkeling
experiences.description: Explore the calm, turquoise waters of Nusa Dua, Bali's most pristine beach area. Rent snorkeling gear and discover vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish just offshore. The protected bay offers ideal conditions for snorkeling, swimming, and simply lounging on immaculate white sand beaches.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Organic Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a traditional organic farm in the Ubud countryside and learn to cook authentic Balinese dishes using freshly harvested ingredients. You'll prepare classics like Nasi Goreng, Satay Lilit, and Lawar while learning about Balinese food culture and Hindu culinary traditions. A deeply enriching cultural and culinary experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take a pre-booked airport shuttle or shared Grab taxi to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud (approx. 1.5–2 hrs, ~IDR 150,000–200,000). Check in to Campuhan Ridge Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk — a scenic 2 km ridge trail through lush green hills, free of charge and perfect for stretching legs after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Jalan Raya Ubud main street. Browse local warungs (small family-run eateries) and settle in for a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: Eaten at airport or on the flight.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at a warung near the airport or upon arrival in Ubud — try Nasi Campur (mixed rice dish) for ~IDR 25,000–35,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka (iconic Ubud spot) or Warung Teges — hearty local meals for ~IDR 35,000–50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange some cash to IDR at the airport or a licensed money changer in Ubud (avoid touts). Carry small bills for warungs.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Campuhan Ridge Walk at sunrise (free). The trail is most beautiful and cool in the early morning with soft golden light over the rice paddies and jungle. Walk takes about 45–60 minutes round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ubud Monkey Forest (Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary) — entry ~IDR 80,000. Explore the ancient temples and lush jungle paths inhabited by hundreds of Balinese long-tailed macaques. Afterward, browse the Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for affordable souvenirs and handcrafted goods.
day_by_day.evening: Watch a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or Arma Open Stage — tickets ~IDR 100,000–150,000. A must-see cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Café Wayan or a local warung near the hotel — banana pancakes and fresh fruit juice for ~IDR 30,000–45,000.
meals.lunch: Warung Ibu Oka or a local rice warung near the Monkey Forest — ~IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Sopa (vegetarian-friendly, affordable) on Sugriwa Street — ~IDR 40,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the ridge walk and Monkey Forest. Keep bags closed and avoid eye contact with monkeys. Book Kecak performance tickets early in the day to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or donation-based morning yoga class — Yoga Barn in Ubud offers community classes from ~IDR 100,000–130,000. Alternatively, Intuitive Flow or Radiantly Alive offer budget drop-in sessions. Focus on a gentle Hatha or Yin class to ease into Bali's yoga scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~IDR 50,000/day) and cycle through the Ubud rice paddies. Head toward Tegallalang Rice Terraces (about 7 km north of Ubud) — entry ~IDR 20,000–50,000 donation. Stunning UNESCO-listed terraced paddies great for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud town. Enjoy a leisurely walk along Jalan Hanoman, a lively street full of cafés, yoga studios, and local shops.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or avocado toast at Kafe Ubud or Morning Glory Café — ~IDR 45,000–65,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Tegallalang — Nasi Goreng or Mie Goreng for ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Locavore To Go (affordable sister restaurant of the famous Locavore) — creative local dishes ~IDR 60,000–90,000.

day_by_day.notes: Cycling to Tegallalang is uphill on the way back — it's a workout! Alternatively, hire a scooter for ~IDR 70,000–80,000/day if cycling feels too strenuous. Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tirta Empul Temple — one of Bali's most sacred water temples, famous for its holy spring purification ritual. Located ~15 km from Ubud (grab a Grab ride ~IDR 40,000 each way). Entry ~IDR 50,000. Observe or respectfully participate in the purification ritual (wear a sarong, provided at entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Gunung Kawi Temple on the way back — ancient 11th-century rock-cut shrines carved into a cliff face. Entry ~IDR 50,000. Explore the lush river valley setting. Return to Ubud and relax at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage in Ubud — many reputable spas offer 1-hour massages for ~IDR 80,000–120,000 (try Jari Menari or local walk-in spas on Jalan Hanoman).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or local warung near Campuhan Ridge — Nasi Goreng and tea ~IDR 25,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Tirta Empul or packed lunch from a local market — ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Pak Malen or any warung on Jalan Dewi Sita — ~IDR 35,000–55,000.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly at temples (shoulders and knees covered). Sarongs and sashes are usually available to rent/borrow at temple entrances. Arrive at Tirta Empul early to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga session at Yoga Barn (drop-in ~IDR 130,000) — try a Vinyasa Flow or Pranayama class. Yoga Barn is one of Southeast Asia's most celebrated yoga centers and is walking distance from central Ubud.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — free entry to the outer courtyard. Admire the traditional Balinese royal architecture. Then explore the Blanco Renaissance Museum (~IDR 80,000 entry) — a stunning museum in the home and studio of eccentric artist Antonio Blanco, with beautiful gardens overlooking the Campuhan River.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Legong or Barong dance performance at Ubud Palace — ~IDR 100,000–150,000. One of the most elegant traditional Balinese dance forms.

meals.breakfast: Juice and granola bowl at Sage Restaurant & Bar (plant-based, affordable) — ~IDR 45,000–65,000.
meals.lunch: Warung on Jalan Monkey Forest — Gado-Gado or Soto Ayam ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Naughty Nuri's Warung (famous for ribs and cocktails — budget-friendly local option) — ~IDR 60,000–90,000.

day_by_day.notes: Yoga Barn has a community board with free or low-cost events, workshops, and meditation sessions — check it when you visit. The Blanco Museum is worth it for the architecture and gardens alone.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the beach! Hire a scooter or book a shared shuttle to Seminyak or Canggu (~1.5 hrs from Ubud, shared shuttle ~IDR 80,000–100,000 one way). Arrive and spend the morning relaxing on the beach — Batu Bolong Beach in Canggu is free, laid-back, and popular with surfers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a beginner surf lesson on Batu Bolong Beach — local instructors offer 1.5–2 hr lessons for ~IDR 150,000–200,000 including board rental. The July swell is ideal for beginners. Alternatively, rent a board and paddle at your own pace (~IDR 50,000–80,000/hr).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Grab a Bintang beer or fresh coconut from a beach vendor (~IDR 20,000–35,000). Take the evening shuttle back to Ubud.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or warung before departure — ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Warung or beach shack in Canggu — fish tacos, nasi goreng, or grilled corn ~IDR 30,000–55,000.
meals.dinner: Eat in Canggu before the return shuttle — Old Man's Bar or a local warung ~IDR 50,000–80,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book the return shuttle in advance or arrange a pickup time with your driver. July weather is warm and dry — perfect beach day. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and stay hydrated. Rip currents can be strong; surf only in flagged zones.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Practice yoga on your own or do gentle stretching on the hotel terrace. Enjoy the peaceful Campuhan Ridge surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Penestanan Village — a quiet artists' village just a 10-minute walk from Campuhan Ridge. Browse local art galleries (many are free to enter) and watch local painters at work. Visit the Sayan Terrace viewpoint for stunning rice terrace and river valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class in Ubud — many affordable classes run in the late afternoon/evening for ~IDR 200,000–300,000 including market visit, cooking, and eating your creations (try Lobong Culinary Experience or Casa Luna Cooking School).

meals.breakfast: Slow morning — fresh fruit, local coffee, and toast at a nearby warung ~IDR 25,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the Ubud traditional market (Pasar Ubud) — fresh tropical fruits, rice cakes, and snacks ~IDR 20,000–30,000.
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations — included in class fee!

day_by_day.notes: The Ubud Traditional Market (Pasar Ubud) is best visited early morning when it's busiest and freshest, but afternoon stalls are also open. Cooking classes often include a morning market visit — check if yours does.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise hike to Mount Batur (Gunung Batur) — depart from Ubud at ~2:00–3:00 AM by pre-arranged transport (~IDR 150,000 round trip). Guided trek to the summit (~IDR 350,000–500,000 including guide, compulsory) takes about 2 hrs. Watch the sunrise from 1,717 m above sea level — one of Bali's most iconic experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and stop at natural hot springs near Lake Batur to soak tired muscles (~IDR 50,000–100,000 entry). Return to Ubud by early afternoon and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening — gentle walk along the Campuhan Ridge at dusk, enjoy the golden hour light.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast on Mount Batur — guides typically provide hard-boiled eggs and bananas cooked in volcanic steam (included in guide fee or ~IDR 30,000 extra).
meals.lunch: Warung near the hot springs or back in Ubud — ~IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Biah Biah on Jalan Goutama — authentic Balinese home cooking, very affordable ~IDR 35,000–55,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Batur trek guide and transport the day before. Bring a warm layer — it's cold at the summit before sunrise (can drop to 10°C). Wear sturdy shoes. This is a long day; plan for an afternoon nap.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and yoga recovery morning. Attend a Yin Yoga or Restorative Yoga class at Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive (~IDR 100,000–130,000) — perfect for post-hike muscle recovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave Temple) — just 4 km east of Ubud, reachable by scooter or Grab (~IDR 25,000). Entry ~IDR 50,000. Explore the ancient 9th-century cave temple, bathing pools, and surrounding jungle. Combine with a short walk to the nearby Petanu River valley.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Ubud's night market area near Jalan Raya Ubud. Browse local street food stalls and pick up cheap snacks and fresh fruit.

meals.breakfast: Açaí bowl or smoothie at Bali Buda Café (health-focused, budget-friendly) — ~IDR 45,000–65,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Goa Gajah — ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Street food at the night market — satay skewers, martabak (stuffed pancake), and fresh juices ~IDR 30,000–50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Day 9 is intentionally light after the Batur hike. Listen to your body. The Yin Yoga class will help with recovery. Goa Gajah requires a sarong (available to borrow at the entrance).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nusa Penida island — take an early shared shuttle from Ubud to Sanur port (~IDR 60,000–80,000), then a fast boat to Nusa Penida (~IDR 150,000–200,000 round trip, 45 min). Rent a scooter on the island (~IDR 80,000/day) and head to Kelingking Beach viewpoint — one of the most photographed spots in Bali. The cliff-top view is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Angel's Billabong and Broken Beach on the western tip of Nusa Penida — stunning natural rock formations and a natural infinity pool. Swim at Crystal Bay (calm, clear water, great for snorkeling — bring your own gear or rent ~IDR 30,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return fast boat to Sanur by 17:00, then shuttle back to Ubud. Arrive by 19:00–20:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — warung near hotel ~IDR 25,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Warung on Nusa Penida near Crystal Bay — simple grilled fish or nasi campur ~IDR 35,000–55,000.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at a warung in Ubud upon return — ~IDR 35,000–50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book the fast boat in advance — July is peak season and boats fill up. The road on Nusa Penida is steep and rough; only ride a scooter if you're confident. Alternatively, hire a local driver for ~IDR 300,000–400,000 for the day. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, cash (limited ATMs on the island), and a dry bag.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tanah Lot Temple at sunrise — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rock formation in the ocean. Located ~35 km from Ubud (~1 hr by scooter or shared transport ~IDR 80,000). Entry ~IDR 60,000. Best visited at low tide when you can walk to the temple base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seminyak Beach for the afternoon — enjoy the white sand beach, people-watch, and take a dip in the warm Indian Ocean. Seminyak is more upscale but the beach itself is free.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the world-famous Seminyak/Kuta sunset from the beach. Head back to Ubud via shuttle or Grab (~IDR 80,000–120,000).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near Tanah Lot — local warung near the temple serves nasi goreng and coffee ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Warung on Seminyak Beach Road — budget warungs are available just off the main beach strip ~IDR 35,000–55,000.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ubud on return — Warung Teges or any local warung ~IDR 35,000–55,000.

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times for Tanah Lot before visiting — the temple is most dramatic and accessible at low tide. July sunsets in Seminyak are spectacular. Avoid the overpriced beach clubs and stick to local warungs for food.

day_by_day.morning: Final yoga morning — book a special 2-hour yoga and meditation workshop at Yoga Barn or Intuitive Flow (~IDR 150,000–200,000). A meaningful way to deepen your practice before leaving Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Ubud Art Market and along Jalan Monkey Forest. Look for handmade silver jewelry, batik fabric, wooden carvings, and essential oils — bargaining is expected and part of the fun. Budget ~IDR 100,000–300,000 for gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell dinner — try Hujan Locale (modern Indonesian cuisine, moderate price ~IDR 100,000–150,000 per person) or Mozaic Warung (affordable sister restaurant of award-winning Mozaic). Reflect on the trip over a Bintang or fresh coconut.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full breakfast at Café Lotus overlooking the lotus pond — ~IDR 50,000–80,000.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a warung — save appetite for farewell dinner ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Hujan Locale or Mozaic Warung — ~IDR 100,000–150,000.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to make Day 13 departure smooth. Keep any liquid souvenirs (essential oils, coconut oil) in checked luggage. Check your flight details and arrange airport transport in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along Campuhan Ridge — one last peaceful stroll through the green hills of Ubud. Take photos, breathe in the fresh morning air, and say goodbye to Bali's magic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Depending on your flight time, either head directly to the airport (arrange Grab or pre-booked shuttle ~IDR 150,000–200,000 to Ngurah Rai Airport, ~1.5–2 hrs) or spend a few final hours in Ubud if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ngurah Rai International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final warung breakfast near Campuhan Ridge — Nasi Goreng, fresh fruit, and Bali coffee ~IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a final warung stop before departure — ~IDR 35,000–60,000.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive to the airport, check-in, and security — Ngurah Rai can be busy in July. Keep some IDR for any last-minute airport purchases or tips. Departure tax is typically included in your ticket.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud Boutique Stay (approx. 1.5–2 hrs drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk — a scenic 9 km ridge trail with sweeping valley views and cool breeze. Perfect low-key introduction to Ubud.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Ubud town centre on foot. Browse the Ubud Art Market for local crafts and souvenirs, then settle in for a relaxed first dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or en route — try a local warung (small Indonesian eatery) for nasi goreng or mie goreng (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Locavore To Go, Ubud — popular mid-range spot serving creative Indonesian-inspired dishes; budget ~IDR 150,000–250,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen even on the ridge walk. Warm summer weather expected — light breathable clothing recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a sunrise yoga class at Yoga Barn, Ubud — one of Bali's most celebrated yoga centres offering Hatha, Vinyasa, and meditation sessions (~IDR 130,000–160,000 per class). Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the sacred Tirta Empul Temple (Holy Spring Water Temple) — a stunning Hindu water temple where locals and visitors participate in purification rituals. Modest dress required (sarong provided at entrance, ~IDR 50,000 donation).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud — a mesmerising cultural show at sunset (~IDR 100,000–150,000 per person).

meals.breakfast: Café Wayan, Ubud — beloved local café with fresh fruit bowls, smoothies, and Balinese breakfast sets (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.lunch: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — famous for Balinese suckling pig (babi guling), a must-try local specialty (~IDR 80,000–120,000)
meals.dinner: Bridges Restaurant, Campuhan — mid-range restaurant with stunning gorge views and international-Balinese fusion menu (~IDR 200,000–300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tirta Empul is about 15 km from Ubud centre — hire a scooter (~IDR 70,000/day) or use a local driver (~IDR 150,000–250,000 for half-day). Bring a change of clothes if participating in the water ritual.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and pranayama session at Radiantly Alive Yoga Studio, Ubud (~IDR 130,000). Afterwards, visit the nearby Saraswati Temple (Lotus Temple) in central Ubud — free entry, beautiful lotus pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ubud Monkey Forest (Mandala Suci Wenara Wana) — a lush nature reserve home to over 700 Balinese long-tailed macaques and ancient temple ruins (~IDR 80,000 entry). Walk the forest trails for 1–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class at Paon Bali Cooking Class — learn to prepare 5–6 traditional Balinese dishes including sate, lawar, and black rice pudding (~IDR 350,000–450,000 including market visit and meal).

meals.breakfast: Kafe, Ubud — healthy plant-based café with açaí bowls, granola, and cold-pressed juices (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.lunch: Warung Teges — authentic local warung near Monkey Forest serving nasi campur (mixed rice) for ~IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Included in the cooking class — enjoy the dishes you prepared!

day_by_day.notes: Do not bring food into Monkey Forest as monkeys can be aggressive. Secure bags and remove dangling jewellery. The cooking class typically starts at 17:00 — confirm timing when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tegallalang Rice Terraces (15 mins from Ubud) — walk the iconic UNESCO-listed stepped terraces at golden hour. Enjoy sweeping views and optional bamboo swing experience (~IDR 50,000–100,000). Entry ~IDR 15,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gunung Kawi Temple — a remarkable 11th-century rock-cut temple complex carved into a cliff face near Tampaksiring (~IDR 50,000 entry). Descend 300 steps into a lush river valley for a truly atmospheric experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud for a traditional Balinese massage at one of the many reputable spas along Hanoman Street (~IDR 100,000–200,000 for 60–90 min). End the evening with a peaceful walk along the Campuhan Ridge at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Sari Organik, Ubud — organic café set amid rice fields serving fresh juices, eggs, and Indonesian breakfast (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near Tegallalang — local nasi goreng or mie goreng with a cold Bintang beer (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Ubud — acclaimed fine-dining restaurant with a seasonal tasting menu; splurge-worthy mid-range option (~IDR 400,000–600,000 per person); book ahead

day_by_day.notes: Hire a driver for the day (~IDR 300,000–400,000) to comfortably cover Tegallalang and Gunung Kawi. Bring cash as many sites are cash-only. Light rain possible in the afternoon — carry a small poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a Yin Yoga or restorative yoga class at The Yoga Barn (~IDR 130,000). Afterwards, explore Ubud's vibrant morning market (Pasar Ubud) — open from 06:00, best visited early for fresh tropical fruit, local snacks, and flowers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Puri Lukisan Museum — Ubud's oldest fine arts museum showcasing traditional Balinese paintings and carvings (~IDR 80,000 entry). Then explore the nearby Blanco Renaissance Museum, former home of Spanish-Balinese artist Don Antonio Blanco (~IDR 80,000).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Legong or Barong Dance performance at Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — held in an open-air courtyard setting (~IDR 100,000–150,000). One of Bali's most authentic cultural performances.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit and jaja (Balinese rice cakes) from Ubud morning market — budget ~IDR 20,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Clear Café, Ubud — popular health-conscious café with raw, vegan, and Balinese options (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.dinner: Warung Ibu Oka 2, Ubud — lighter option post-performance; nasi campur and satay (~IDR 60,000–100,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Ubud morning market transitions to tourist stalls after 09:00 — arrive by 07:00–08:00 for the authentic local experience. Ubud Palace performances usually start at 19:30; arrive 20 mins early for good seats.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer south to Seminyak/Canggu area (approx. 1.5 hrs from Ubud) for a beach-focused day. Check into a day hotel or beach club. Start with a morning surf lesson at Echo Beach, Canggu — beginner-friendly waves; lessons ~IDR 250,000–350,000 including board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and sunbathe at Batu Bolong Beach, Canggu — one of Bali's most picturesque and laid-back beaches. Rent a sun lounger (~IDR 50,000) and soak in the warm July sun. Explore the beachside cafés and boutiques along the Canggu strip.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Bali sunset at La Brisa or Old Man's beach bar in Canggu — iconic sunset spots with live music, cocktails, and beach vibes. Return to Ubud by private driver after sunset.

meals.breakfast: On the road — stop at a local warung in Ubud before departure or eat at Canggu upon arrival
meals.lunch: Betelnut Café, Canggu — healthy bowls, burgers, and smoothies with a beachside vibe (~IDR 100,000–180,000)
meals.dinner: Warung Dandelion, Canggu — beloved local spot with affordable Balinese and Western dishes before the drive back (~IDR 80,000–150,000)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the day (~IDR 400,000–500,000 return) for flexibility. July is peak surf season in Canggu — conditions are generally excellent. Apply SPF 50+ sunscreen. Stay hydrated throughout the beach day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — enjoy a gentle Hatha yoga session at your boutique stay (check if the property offers in-house sessions) or return to Yoga Barn. Take a slow morning walk along the Campuhan Ridge to reconnect with nature.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Penestanan village — the 'artists' village' just a short walk from Campuhan Ridge. Explore local galleries, watch artisans at work, and browse handmade textiles and silverwork. A peaceful, crowd-free alternative to central Ubud.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a traditional Balinese boreh (herbal body scrub) and flower bath at a local spa such as Taksu Spa or Karsa Spa (~IDR 250,000–400,000 for a 90-min package). Perfect mid-trip rejuvenation.

meals.breakfast: Seniman Coffee Studio, Ubud — specialty coffee, avocado toast, and fresh pastries (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.lunch: Warung Sopa, Ubud — popular vegetarian and vegan warung with generous portions (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Bridges Restaurant, Campuhan — revisit for their excellent cocktails and gorge-view dining (~IDR 200,000–300,000)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter — a mid-trip rest day is important for a balanced itinerary. Use this time to do laundry, recharge devices, journal, or simply relax at the boutique stay.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise trek to Mount Batur (Gunung Batur) — depart from Ubud at 02:00 AM to reach the summit by sunrise (~05:30). Trek with a certified guide (~IDR 300,000–450,000 per person including guide and breakfast at summit). Breathtaking panoramic views over Lake Batur.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending, visit the natural hot springs at Toya Devasya or Batur Natural Hot Spring (~IDR 150,000–300,000 entry) — the perfect post-trek soak with views of the volcano. Return to Ubud by early afternoon for rest.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening — gentle stretch or restorative yoga, then an early dinner and rest after the pre-dawn trek.

meals.breakfast: Simple breakfast provided by guide at Batur summit — typically eggs, toast, and coffee/tea
meals.lunch: Warung near Kintamani — local nasi campur or soto ayam (chicken soup) with lake views (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Naughty Nuri's Warung, Ubud — famous for BBQ ribs and cold Bintang; casual and satisfying post-trek meal (~IDR 150,000–250,000)

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur trek requires an early 02:00 departure from Ubud. Book a reputable trekking agency in advance (e.g., Batur Trekking, Bali Sunrise Trekking). Bring a warm layer — summit temperatures can drop to 10–15°C before sunrise. Wear sturdy shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Amed, East Bali — a 1.5–2 hr drive from Ubud. Amed is a peaceful coastal village renowned for its black sand beaches and world-class snorkelling. Morning snorkel at the famous Japanese Shipwreck — a WWII-era wreck in shallow water teeming with marine life. Snorkel gear rental ~IDR 50,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the traditional salt-making villages of Amed — one of the last places in Bali where salt is still made by hand using traditional palm-trunk troughs. Visit a local salt farmer and learn about the centuries-old process. Relax on the quiet Amed beach in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront café in Amed with views of Mount Agung across the water. Drive back to Ubud or stay overnight in Amed (optional — budget guesthouses available from ~IDR 200,000/night).

meals.breakfast: Pack a light breakfast from a Ubud café before departure or eat en route
meals.lunch: Warung Enak, Amed — local seafood warung with fresh grilled fish, calamari, and cold drinks with ocean views (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.dinner: Sama Sama Reggae Bar & Warung, Amed — relaxed beachside dinner with fresh catch of the day (~IDR 100,000–180,000) before returning to Ubud

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Amed day trip (~IDR 450,000–550,000 return). The road to Amed is winding — allow extra travel time. Amed is significantly quieter than south Bali — a wonderful contrast to busier areas. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Vinyasa flow yoga class at Radiantly Alive or Yoga Barn (~IDR 130,000). Afterwards, visit Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) — a 9th-century archaeological site and Hindu sanctuary just 4 km from Ubud (~IDR 50,000 entry). Explore the cave, bathing pools, and surrounding jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seminyak Beach for an afternoon of beach relaxation. Rent a sun lounger at Ku De Ta Beach Club or W Bali Seminyak — both offer stunning beachfront settings with pools, cocktails, and world-class service. Day pass ~IDR 200,000–300,000 (redeemable against food/drinks).
day_by_day.evening: Seminyak sunset at Potato Head Beach Club — one of Bali's most iconic sunset venues with a stunning amphitheatre-style pool facing the Indian Ocean. Cocktails from ~IDR 100,000. Return to Ubud by private driver.

meals.breakfast: Alchemy Café, Ubud — raw vegan superfood bowls and smoothies; ideal pre-yoga fuel (~IDR 80,000–140,000)
meals.lunch: Merah Putih, Seminyak — beautiful upscale Indonesian restaurant in a stunning bamboo-and-glass structure; mid-range splurge (~IDR 250,000–400,000)
meals.dinner: La Lucciola, Seminyak — romantic beachfront Italian-Indonesian restaurant with excellent pasta and seafood (~IDR 200,000–350,000)

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is approx. 1.5 hrs from Ubud — plan for a full day trip. Seminyak beach is calmer than Kuta but still has strong currents — swim between the flags. Dress smartly for beach clubs (no torn clothing or flip-flops at some venues).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most photographed sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop (~IDR 60,000 entry). Best visited in the morning to avoid crowds. Explore the surrounding cliffs, rock formations, and temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Uluwatu Temple (Pura Luhur Uluwatu) on the Bukit Peninsula — a dramatic clifftop temple 70 m above the Indian Ocean (~IDR 50,000 entry). Walk the cliff-edge path with stunning ocean panoramas. Watch out for cheeky monkeys!
day_by_day.evening: Attend the famous Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu Temple — performed at sunset on a clifftop stage with the ocean as a backdrop; one of Bali's most spectacular cultural experiences (~IDR 150,000). Dinner in Jimbaran Bay — famous for its seafood warungs on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Café Biku, Seminyak/Ubud — charming heritage café with Balinese-style eggs benedict and fresh juices (~IDR 100,000–160,000)
meals.lunch: Single Fin, Uluwatu — iconic clifftop café/bar overlooking Suluban Beach with burgers, salads, and cold Bintang (~IDR 120,000–200,000)
meals.dinner: Jimbaran Bay seafood BBQ — choose your fresh seafood (lobster, prawns, fish) by weight, grilled on the beach with rice and sambal; ~IDR 200,000–400,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a full south Bali day — hire a driver for the day (~IDR 500,000–600,000). Tanah Lot is best at low tide. Uluwatu Kecak Dance starts at approximately 18:00 — arrive by 17:30. Jimbaran Bay is a 20-min drive from Uluwatu.

day_by_day.morning: Final yoga session in Ubud — choose a special class such as aerial yoga or sound healing meditation at Yoga Barn (~IDR 150,000–200,000). A meaningful way to honour your yoga journey in Bali before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and exploration in Ubud — visit Jalan Dewi Sita and Jalan Hanoman for boutique shops selling handmade jewellery, batik textiles, organic beauty products, and Balinese art. Pick up meaningful souvenirs and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special Ubud restaurant. Stroll the Campuhan Ridge one final time at dusk for a peaceful goodbye to Ubud's magical landscape.

meals.breakfast: Room Café, Ubud — cosy café with excellent granola, fresh fruit platters, and Bali coffee (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.lunch: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — revisit this Ubud classic for one last babi guling before leaving (~IDR 80,000–120,000)
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Ubud or Bridges Restaurant — splurge on a memorable farewell dinner with fine Balinese cuisine and excellent wine (~IDR 350,000–600,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to repack and ensure all souvenirs are safely wrapped. Confirm airport transfer for Day 13. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the final evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Campuhan Ridge Walk. Breathe in the fresh Ubud air, listen to the sounds of the jungle, and savour the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique stay. Depending on flight time, stop at a final café in Ubud or en route to the airport. Private transfer from Campuhan Ridge, Ubud to Ngurah Rai International Airport (allow 2–2.5 hrs including check-in time).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry beautiful memories of rice terraces, sacred temples, ocean sunsets, and transformative yoga sessions.

meals.breakfast: Seniman Coffee Studio — one last specialty coffee and light breakfast before checkout (~IDR 70,000–100,000)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at Ubud or airport — Nasi goreng at a warung (~IDR 40,000–60,000) or airport dining (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Ubud-to-airport transfer, especially during peak July traffic. Pre-book your airport transfer the night before. Ensure you have IDR cash for any last-minute tips, offerings, or purchases. Departure tax is included in most international tickets.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud Boutique Stay. Check in, settle into your luxury suite, and enjoy a welcome drink and spa foot ritual offered by the property. Take a leisurely stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk to soak in the lush green hillside scenery and decompress after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private villa terrace or the hotel's infinity pool overlooking the jungle canopy. Gentle orientation walk through Campuhan village to discover the local ambiance.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: N/A — en route from airport; light snacks provided during transfer
meals.dinner: Bridges Bali Restaurant, Campuhan — a landmark fine-dining venue perched over the Wos River gorge, renowned for its contemporary European-Asian cuisine, premium wine list, and dramatic candlelit setting

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed. Confirm spa bookings and any excursion reservations with the concierge upon check-in. Hydrate well after the flight; Bali's warm humidity (avg. 25°C) can be deceptive.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the hotel's open-air shala overlooking the Campuhan Ridge — a private instructor can be arranged through the concierge. Follow with a nourishing breakfast. Afterward, walk the full Campuhan Ridge Trail (approx. 9 km round trip) through swaying alang-alang grasslands and traditional compounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ARMA (Agung Rai Museum of Art) in Ubud to explore Balinese classical and modern art across beautifully landscaped pavilions. Enjoy a traditional Balinese painting workshop included with premium entry.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the world-famous Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or Pura Taman Saraswati — a mesmerizing traditional Balinese ritual performance held at sunset. Return to the hotel for a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — full gourmet Balinese breakfast with fresh tropical fruits, jamu shots, eggs to order, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Swept Away at COMO Shambhala Estate — organic, locally sourced cuisine in a stunning riverside jungle setting
meals.dinner: Locavore, Ubud — one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, offering a creative tasting menu built entirely on Indonesian ingredients with exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book Locavore well in advance; reservations fill up weeks ahead. The Kecak Dance at Pura Dalem Ubud begins around 19:30 — check exact timing with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and pranayama session at the hotel followed by a guided meditation. After breakfast, visit Pura Tirta Empul — the sacred Hindu water temple where locals perform purification rituals in the holy spring pools. Dress respectfully; sarongs provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the terraced rice fields of Tegalalang (a short drive from Ubud) — one of Bali's most photogenic UNESCO-recognized subak irrigation landscapes. Enjoy a private guided walk through the paddies with a local farmer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a 90-minute Balinese traditional massage and body scrub at the in-house spa. Enjoy a quiet, romantic dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — tropical smoothie bowls, house-baked pastries, and cold-brew coffee
meals.lunch: Sari Organik, Tegalalang — a beloved farm-to-table restaurant nestled in the rice terraces, serving fresh organic Balinese dishes with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Room service or in-hotel dining — request the chef's private dinner experience on your terrace under the stars (arrange through concierge)

day_by_day.notes: Tirta Empul requires modest dress — shoulders and knees covered. Arrive before 09:00 to beat the crowds. Tegalalang can be busy midday; the guided walk takes you off the main tourist paths.

day_by_day.morning: Yin yoga class at the hotel followed by a Balinese jamu herbal elixir tasting. Private driver excursion to Mount Batur — a 1,717m active volcano — for a guided sunrise trek (depart hotel ~03:30 to reach the summit by sunrise ~06:00). Witness breathtaking views over Lake Batur and the caldera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and soak in the natural hot springs at Toya Devasya Batur — a premium hot spring resort at the base of the volcano with private pools and lake views. Enjoy a leisurely lunch on-site before returning to Ubud.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle restorative yoga session back at the hotel to ease the muscles after the trek. Relax with a glass of Balinese wine on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek — packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the hotel (sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, thermos of coffee)
meals.lunch: Toya Devasya Hot Springs Resort restaurant — fresh grilled fish, satay platters, and tropical juices overlooking Lake Batur
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique, Ubud — a celebrated fine-dining institution in a magical garden setting, offering French-inspired tasting menus with Balinese ingredients and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The Batur trek is moderately strenuous — wear sturdy shoes and bring a light jacket for the cool summit. Depart no later than 03:30 from the hotel. Book the guide and hot springs in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, then enjoy a leisurely in-hotel breakfast. Gentle morning flow yoga on the shala. Explore the boutique galleries and artisan workshops of Campuhan and the nearby Penestanan artists' village on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private batik or silver jewelry-making workshop with a local Ubud artisan master — a deeply immersive cultural experience. Browse the Ubud Art Market for premium hand-crafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at Night Rooster or CP Lounge rooftop bar in central Ubud with panoramic views. Dinner in the heart of Ubud.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — eggs Benedict with smoked duck, fresh papaya, and turmeric latte
meals.lunch: Hujan Locale, Ubud — a sophisticated restaurant celebrating the diverse regional cuisines of the Indonesian archipelago with a curated cocktail menu
meals.dinner: Room at Alaya Resort Ubud — elegant open-air restaurant with refined Balinese cuisine, creative cocktails, and live acoustic music

day_by_day.notes: The Ubud Art Market is best visited in the morning when vendors are freshest and prices more negotiable. The artisan workshop should be pre-booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer south to the Bukit Peninsula (approx. 2 hours). Check into a day-use luxury beach club or arrange a private villa day pass. Morning yoga session on the cliffs above the Indian Ocean at a clifftop studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Karma Beach Club, Karma Kandara — accessible by private funicular down to a secluded white-sand beach. Swim in crystal-clear turquoise water, enjoy a private cabana, and snorkel in the reef.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at Single Fin Bar, Uluwatu — perched on the clifftop with sweeping views of the famous surf break. Watch surfers ride the legendary waves as the sun sets over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Ubud — light continental breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Karma Beach Club restaurant — fresh seafood platters, lobster rolls, tropical salads, and premium cocktails with toes in the sand
meals.dinner: Cuca Restaurant, Jimbaran — an award-winning tapas-style restaurant using locally sourced Balinese produce with inventive global techniques; book the chef's table for the full experience

day_by_day.notes: This is a day trip from Ubud — your hotel can arrange a premium private driver for the full day. Karma Beach requires a reservation or day pass. Pack reef-safe sunscreen and a beach bag. July weather is ideal — minimal rain, warm and sunny.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Tanah Lot sea temple at low tide — one of Bali's most sacred and photographed landmarks, perched dramatically on a rocky outcrop in the sea. Arrive early (around 08:00) to avoid crowds and catch the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Seminyak Beach — Bali's most glamorous beach strip. Spend the afternoon at Potato Head Beach Club (Potahto) — a design-forward luxury beach club with a stunning infinity pool, private sun loungers, and world-class DJs.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll Seminyak's boutique-lined streets for premium Balinese fashion and homewares shopping. Sunset cocktails at La Plancha beach bar — colorful bean bags on the sand as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: En route — stop at a local warung near Tanah Lot for a traditional Balinese breakfast of nasi jinggo and fresh coconut
meals.lunch: Potato Head Beach Club — elevated Indonesian and international cuisine with fresh juices and signature cocktails in a stunning poolside setting
meals.dinner: Merah Putih, Seminyak — a stunning architectural masterpiece restaurant serving refined modern Indonesian cuisine across 10 regional culinary traditions; one of Bali's best dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Return to Ubud hotel in the evening (approx. 1.5-hour drive). Alternatively, consider a one-night luxury stay in Seminyak if you wish to extend the beach experience — discuss with concierge. Tanah Lot is best at low tide; check tide times in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-morning luxury spa retreat at COMO Shambhala Estate — one of Asia's premier wellness sanctuaries. Book the signature COMO Shambhala Journey (3 hours): includes Ayurvedic consultation, herbal steam, full-body massage, and scalp treatment in a stunning riverside jungle setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum — the flamboyant former home and studio of Catalan-Balinese artist Antonio Blanco, set in a dramatic hillside garden above the Campuhan River. Explore the collection of romantic and erotic Balinese-inspired paintings.
day_by_day.evening: Private traditional Balinese cooking class with a local chef — learn to prepare a five-course Balinese feast using fresh market ingredients, including lawar, bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck), and black rice pudding.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — full Balinese breakfast with jamu shots and fresh fruit platter
meals.lunch: COMO Shambhala Estate — post-spa organic wellness lunch with cold-pressed juices, grain bowls, and raw desserts
meals.dinner: The dishes you prepared in your cooking class — enjoy a private candlelit dinner at the hotel or a dedicated dining space arranged by the class host

day_by_day.notes: COMO Shambhala treatments must be booked well in advance — the concierge can assist. The cooking class typically runs 17:00–20:00 and includes a market visit option in the morning if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga and breathwork session on the Campuhan Ridge — private instructor at the hotel. After breakfast, visit Pura Besakih — the 'Mother Temple' of Bali, dramatically set on the slopes of sacred Mount Agung (approx. 1.5-hour drive). The largest and holiest Hindu temple complex on the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the scenic Lake Batur viewpoint in Kintamani on the return journey — enjoy panoramic volcanic caldera views. Visit a traditional Balinese coffee plantation for a luwak coffee tasting and tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Relax with a private sunset yoga nidra session at the hotel. Quiet evening in.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and cold-brew coffee
meals.lunch: Gunawan Restaurant, Kintamani — a cliff-edge restaurant with sweeping views over Lake Batur and Mount Abang; enjoy a buffet of Balinese and Indonesian dishes
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka, Ubud — the legendary suckling pig (babi guling) institution beloved by Anthony Bourdain; a must-try authentic Balinese experience even for luxury travelers

day_by_day.notes: Besakih requires a local guide (mandatory) and modest dress. Arrive before 10:00 to avoid the midday heat and tour groups. The coffee plantation stop adds about 45 minutes to the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise beach yoga session — arrange a full-day transfer to the pristine beaches of Nusa Dua. Begin with a yoga class on the beach at a five-star resort (St. Regis Bali or Mulia Resort offer day passes). Swim in calm, sheltered turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Water sports and beach leisure at Nusa Dua — try stand-up paddleboarding, parasailing, or a glass-bottom boat tour over the coral reef. Relax on a private beach cabana.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Jimbaran Bay for the quintessential Bali seafood-on-the-beach experience. Watch the sun set over the bay as you dine on grilled lobster and fresh catch.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Ubud — light breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Kayuputi Restaurant, St. Regis Bali, Nusa Dua — one of Bali's most elegant beachfront restaurants, offering contemporary Southeast Asian cuisine with a premium wine list and Indian Ocean views
meals.dinner: Jimbaran Bay seafood — book a premium table at Sundara Beach Club (Four Seasons Jimbaran Bay) for an elevated version of the famous beach seafood experience with white-glove service

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Dua is approximately 1.5 hours from Ubud. A full-day private driver is recommended. The beaches here are calm and ideal for swimming — perfect contrast to Seminyak's surf. Return to Ubud hotel in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike to the hidden waterfall of Tibumana or Kanto Lampo (both within 30 minutes of Ubud) — a magical jungle experience with emerald pools and dramatic cascades. Swim in the natural pools. Return for a late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full afternoon of leisure at the hotel — use of pool, in-room treatments, or a private Balinese floral bath ritual. Alternatively, visit the Ubud Botanic Garden (Kebun Raya Bali) in nearby Bedugul — a stunning highland garden at 1,400m altitude with rare orchid collections.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private full-moon or celestial ceremony blessing at a local temple (if timing aligns — July 2027 full moon: July 11, so a waning moon ceremony may be available). Enjoy a farewell-style luxury dinner.

meals.breakfast: Post-hike — in-hotel brunch: eggs royale, fresh juices, and Balinese black rice porridge
meals.lunch: Sari Organik, Ubud — return visit or try Alchemy Ubud for a premium raw vegan feast with superfood smoothie bowls
meals.dinner: Apéritif Restaurant, Ubud — a theatrical, immersive fine-dining experience inspired by the golden age of cocktail culture; set in a stunning colonial mansion with a world-class cocktail program and seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall hikes are best done early morning before the heat. Wear water shoes and bring a dry bag. Apéritif is one of Ubud's most celebrated restaurants — reservations essential and should be made weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga and meditation session at the hotel — a reflective, closing practice. After a leisurely breakfast, explore the Campuhan neighborhood one last time — visit the Neka Art Museum for an in-depth look at the history of Balinese painting across seven pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute premium shopping in Ubud — visit Goddess on the Go for luxury resort wear, Kou Cuisine for artisan Balinese skincare, and Threads of Life for UNESCO-recognized traditional textiles. Enjoy a final spa treatment — a Balinese boreh (spice body wrap) and scalp massage.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails at the hotel terrace. Private candlelit farewell dinner at the hotel — request the chef's special tasting menu with wine pairing as a closing celebration of the journey.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — full gourmet spread: freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit, smoked salmon, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant, Ubud — a chic, plant-forward eatery with a creative menu of grain bowls, house-made ferments, and natural wines
meals.dinner: In-hotel private chef's dinner on the terrace — arrange with the hotel for a bespoke multi-course Balinese-inspired tasting menu with premium wine pairings and live gamelan music

day_by_day.notes: Pack thoughtfully — many artisan purchases may need careful wrapping. Check airline baggage allowances for batik, textiles, and ceramics. Confirm departure transfer time with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake at leisure. Gentle stretching or a short solo walk along the Campuhan Ridge for one last look at the emerald valley. Enjoy a final Balinese breakfast at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out and private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the Ubud-to-airport journey (traffic can be heavy). Airport lounge access recommended for a comfortable pre-flight experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the serenity of Bali home with you.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — final tropical breakfast: fresh papaya with lime, nasi goreng, and a farewell jamu shot
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or a light meal at the airport — Ngurah Rai has several quality dining options post-security
meals.dinner: In-flight

day_by_day.notes: Ubud to Bali airport can take 1.5 to 2.5 hours depending on traffic — always allow extra time. Request a late checkout (12:00 or 13:00) from the hotel if your flight is in the afternoon or evening. Purchase any last-minute Balinese coffee, chocolate, or spices at the airport as premium gifts.

query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA
